blocks.text: To ensure high availability and fault tolerance by providing alternate paths to reach applications during Network Connector node failures and Network Connector to VPN Service Edge path or link failures, Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) relies on external routers called BGP peers. Peering occurs when BGP peers form connections with other BGP peers. If a failure occurs on a Network Connector within a Network Connector group, VPN Service Edges use peering to reroute traffic to another Network Connector for the specific IP address subnet.
You can configure BGP at a global level. To learn more, see Configuring Border Gateway Protocols for Network Connectors and Configuring a Border Gateway Protocol for a Network Connector.
BGP is enabled when the Advertise LAN Segments Locally option is disabled for a Network Connector group.
External routers provide the following benefits and enable you to:

blocks.item: Ensure continuous communication between the client and server.
Achieve redundancy in the event of failures.

blocks.text: On the External Routers page (Private Access > VPN (for Legacy Apps) > External Routers), you can do the following:

blocks.item: View a list of all configured external routers. For each external router, you can view:
Name: The name of the external router.
Router AS Number: The autonomous system number (ASN) assigned to the external router.
Router IP Address: The IP address assigned to the router.
MD5: The BGP MD5 authentication password. The same value is configured on other BGP peers.
Modify the columns displayed in the table.
Display more rows or a different page of the table.
